about: Issue #4038 (slice 9b), from the decision of 2026-11-21 on #4037: Core publishes an ip-set or ip-aggregate member only as one address or one prefix, in one spelling, and the Outpost loads a line only when pf reads it as one entry.

members: each row is run through Core's canonical member function (go/pfb_core/update/apply, Member) and through the Outpost's member check (pfb_outpost_ip_member_valid() in pfblockerng.inc, tests/php/IpMembersFixtureTest.php). outpost is the check's verdict on member as written. canonical is what Core publishes for it, or null when Core leaves the row out with an issue. A canonical member is always one the check accepts, and a row the check refuses is never published.
The spelling is what Go's netip.Prefix.Masked() prints: a bare address for a host, address/length without host bits for a prefix, IPv6 in lower case with the longest run of zero groups compressed.

The address guard is today's (pfb_sanitize_ipaddr() and pfb_sanitize_ipaddr_v6() in pfblockerng.inc, issue #1922), judged on the network pf loads: an IPv4 network whose first octet is 0, the IPv6 network ::, and a prefix length of 0 are left out.

ipset_departures: the lists of go/pfb_core/ipset/testdata/ipset.json that Core publishes (a canonical set, an Uber aggregate, the canonical sets and aggregates of a pipeline pass) whose published body differs from today's: old_expect is the corpus's answer, expect the body Core publishes from it (sorted and unique). A list not named here is published as it is.
